title: Capacity of the binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel
decision_reason: Exact formulation, independent corroboration, full resolution-scope comparisons, duplicate review, separated A48 adversarial self-review and repository/rendering checks passed; no unresolved material matching resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.model: Two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel, one sender, binary input X and binary outputs Y,Z; no feedback or receiver cooperation.
problem_fingerprint.transition_law: Rows indexed by X=0,1 and columns by output=0,1: P(Y|X)=[[1,0],[1/2,1/2]], P(Z|X)=[[1/2,1/2],[0,1]]. Their product gives the joint transition law; one output is deterministic for each input, so these marginals already determine the joint law.
problem_fingerprint.messages: Two independent uniform private messages, one intended for each receiver; no separately required common message.
problem_fingerprint.codes: For each block length n, arbitrary encoder f_n:[M_1,n] x [M_2,n] -> {0,1}^n and separate decoders g_1,n(Y^n), g_2,n(Z^n). No efficiency, linearity, input-cost or fixed input-distribution restriction.
problem_fingerprint.rates_and_error: Closure of all R_1,R_2 >=0 achievable with liminf_n n^(-1) log_2 M_i,n >= R_i and P(g_1,n(Y^n) != W_1 or g_2,n(Z^n) != W_2) ->0.
problem_fingerprint.target: Determine the exact private-message capacity region, with matching achievability and converse. Characterizing an inner bound or only numerically improving an outer bound is insufficient.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_scope: One canonical fixed channel with crossover/noisy probability 1/2. Other crossover probabilities, sum capacity, and Marton optimality are not additional entries.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Bits per channel use; n tends to infinity, average error under uniform independent messages.
problem_fingerprint.mathematical_distinctions: Not Gaussian broadcast with noiseless causal feedback (310), interactive two-way multiplication (142), cooperative relay transmission (143), or worst-case binary-code separation.

applied_significance: Foundational throughput region for one sender serving two users with complementary symbol-dependent noise. Resolves a canonical test of multiuser broadcast coding; no claim of a particular deployed communication technology.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Earlier proof withdrawn; v3 gives a new proof and corrected outer-bound computation.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: The resolved claim is an auxiliary mutual-information inequality. The full capacity region remains the target; later published GJNW13 supports the bound evaluation.
resolution_comparisons.disposition: Does not resolve target; historical version issue explicitly retained.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Binary information inequality and exact Marton sum-rate evaluation; strict separation from UV and Körner–Marton upper regions.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Optimality within a specified inner bound does not prove optimality among all codes.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Weighted inequality and simple description of the full Marton region for fixed BSSC; a related broader inequality has a counterexample.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Describes an inner region, not the operational capacity region. The broader counterexample does not settle this fixed channel.
resolution_comparisons.disposition: No resolution or unresolved matching proof claim.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Local tensorization for a product with a binary component.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Full statement only establishes the relevant local/second-order conditions. Global tensorization or global optimizer control needed for capacity is not supplied.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Equivalent superposition-coding descriptions A=B=C, plus algorithms and conditional convergence for evaluating inner and outer regions.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: The letter C in Lemma 1 denotes a representation of an inner bound. Neither that equivalence, a numerical optimizer, nor exact evaluation of one bound closes the achievability-converse gap. Full concavity/initial-point hypotheses retained.
resolution_comparisons.disposition: Does not resolve target; independent explicit open-status assessment.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: J-auxiliary-receiver outer bound improves on UV for some channels.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Necessary inequalities with auxiliary constraints; does not assert their achievability for BSSC. Its strict-improvement example is a different three-input erasure Blackwell channel.
resolution_comparisons.disposition: Applicable outer-bound development, not capacity formula.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: A two-auxiliary bound and reported numerical improvement from about 0.36931657 to 0.36929634 for the 1/2-BSSC.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Still above Marton's 0.36164288 sum rate; author explicitly calls sum capacity unknown. Separate 0.9-channel calculation is not the target. No numerical proof certification claimed.

resolution_comparisons.locator: June v1: Definitions 1–3, Lemma 5 and full Theorem 4; compared separately with January manuscript
resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Capacity region for disjoint sums under three alternatives for weight-dependent primary classes, including less-noisy, more-capable and semi-deterministic components.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: For binary BSSC the only nontrivial input partition separates 0 and 1, but Y=0 and Z=1 each have positive probability under both inputs. Hence Definition 3's output-disjoint sum hypothesis fails. Treating BSSC alone as a full primary component would, by Lemma 5, force Marton/UVW equality, contrary to the known private-message gap. The paper's separate sum-channel gap example does not concern this fixed BSSC.
resolution_comparisons.disposition: Different channel class; mismatch verified from definitions rather than title.

resolution_comparisons.claim_or_result: Explicit capacity with and without feedback and transmission cost for a BSSC.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Binary State Symmetric Channel: one output stream with unit memory and state determined by current input and previous output. The target is Binary Skew-Symmetric Broadcast Channel: two output streams, separate private messages, and a memoryless law.
resolution_comparisons.disposition: Acronym collision, not a matching capacity resolution.

mathematical_checks: Both 2x2 matrices have nonnegative rows summing to one. For each input one receiver output is deterministic, so the marginal matrices uniquely determine the joint law.
Equivalent source convention TY|X=[[1/2,1/2],[0,1]], TZ|X=[[1,0],[1/2,1/2]] is obtained by swapping the two receiver labels; the symmetric capacity region question is unchanged.
Encoder sees both independent messages but no past outputs. Separate decoders, average block error and unrestricted input distribution agree with N20 §1.1.
Two private messages do not prohibit a common auxiliary code layer. No extra common-message rate is required.
Numerical source units checked: D24 §5.5 distinguishes 0.2506717 nats from 0.3616428 bits.
Known inequalities characterize inner and outer bounds. Equality of Marton and UV regions is known false; the draft does not ask to prove it.
All crossover variants and the sum-rate objective belong to this single canonical family; only one accepted addition may result.

closest.difference: Real Gaussian output, block-power constraint and causal noiseless feedback; target here is a fixed finite alphabet channel without feedback.
Two adaptive transmitters exchanging messages; not one broadcaster with separate receiving terminals.
Single message with causal relay cooperation; target has two messages and noncooperating receivers.
Worst-case minimum Hamming distance, not average vanishing-error broadcast capacity.

duplicate_review.counting_rule: One canonical BSSC private-message capacity problem, no separate sum capacity, parameter or Marton-optimality entry.
